facts.text: Serve the mains when Kris shares Thanksgiving dinner with Doris and Susan.
facts.why: There is no Thanksgiving dinner with Kris in the film. Thanksgiving is only the morning of the Macy's parade, when Doris talks Kris into playing Santa. Kris, Fred, Doris and Susan next meet on Christmas Day at his home. The printed card cue is the same line.
facts.fix: Serve the mains when Fred talks his way into Doris's Thanksgiving dinner.

facts.why: False alarm. Doris does host Thanksgiving dinner: Susan wangles Fred an invitation and Doris is cooking it when she gets back from the parade (AFI catalogue synopsis). Kris is not there, which the cue and note now say.

facts.text: the Thanksgiving Kris spends with Doris and Susan
facts.why: Kris does not spend Thanksgiving with Doris and Susan. He meets Doris on the morning of the parade, and meets Susan later at the store.
facts.fix: the Thanksgiving dinner Fred talks his way into

facts.text: Mother says dinner has to come before presents. I don't love the rule, but this smells too good to argue.
facts.why: Printed in quote marks as Susan's words, but she never says it, and no dinner before presents rule appears in the plot. Susan's real arc is a girl raised not to believe in fairy tales who comes round at the end. I could not open a quote page for this pass (the search tool was out of budget), so there is no quote source. A note in her voice that fits the plot is safer.
facts.fix: Mother says I'm too old for fairy tales. I'm having the pudding anyway, in case Santa asks.

fix_note.text: Mother says I'm too old for fairy tales. I'm having the pudding anyway, in case Santa asks.

vibe.verdict: A warm department store tea room with the right letters and parade, but the dinner it builds the cue around never happens in the film.
